what: Timeout signaling targets only the recorded top-level PID
scenario_or_breakage: When a Family B script is blocked inside a foreground child command, such as ship-pr.sh waiting on ci-wait.sh or another helper, killing only the shell PID can still leave the active child process running as an orphan, so the proposed fix does not fully close the leak it is meant to address
suggested_fix: Add process-tree cleanup to the contract: either record and signal an isolated process group/session, or add a tested TERM cleanup path that terminates descendant processes; add a regression fake script that spawns a long-lived child and verify no child remains after monitor timeout

what: The PID-file writer is less strict than the monitor validator
scenario_or_breakage: Monitor-side validation rejects paths outside session tmpdirs and symlinks, but the new lib-quiet helper is planned to write to any absolute no-dotdot path before the foreground monitor can reject its argv; a malformed or hostile LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE could clobber an arbitrary writable file via the predictable tmp path and mv
suggested_fix: Make larch_quiet_write_paired_pid_file enforce the same session-tmpdir, symlink, regular-file, and parent-directory constraints before writing; use mktemp in the target directory instead of a predictable .tmp.$$ name; warn and return 0 on invalid paths so callers do not abort under set -e

what: The proposed allocation check can pass on a bare export without allocation
scenario_or_breakage: The plan says has_pid_alloc should match either LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE=.*mktemp or export LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE, so a fence that only exports an unset or inherited variable can satisfy CI while still lacking a per-launch pid-file allocation
suggested_fix: Require an actual assignment from mktemp before the anchor, plus export, or require a single export assignment such as export LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE="$(mktemp ...)" under the session breadcrumbs directory; add a negative fixture with only export LARCH_PAIRED_PID_FILE to lock this down
